text: Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid) acts as an irreversible inhibitor of PTGS2 (COX-2) by acetylating a specific serine residue (Ser516) within the enzyme's active site, thereby blocking the conversion of arachidonic acid into pro-inflammatory prostaglandins. In the context of colorectal cancer, this inhibition suppresses the prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) signaling pathway, which otherwise promotes tumor cell proliferation, angiogenesis, and resistance to apoptosis. Consequently, chronic low-dose aspirin use is clinically recognized for its chemopreventive efficacy in reducing the incidence and mortality of colorectal adenomas and carcinomas.
